utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hi there. What's been happening since we last met?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: So I need to tell you about something that happened to my coworker. She told me that her ex-boyfriend threatened to hurt her. She doesn't know what to do and asked for my advice. He apparently said he knows where she lives.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That's a concerning situation for your coworker. How did you feel hearing that from her?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Scared for her. I told her she should go to the police. He sounds dangerous. Apparently he threatened to kill her if she didn't come back to him. She's terrified.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That sounds like a serious domestic violence situation. You gave your coworker good advice about the police. How is being a confidant in this situation affecting you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: It's weighing on me. I feel responsible. I've been thinking about her safety all week. I keep wondering if I should do something more. But it's not my situation to handle directly.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Secondary trauma from supporting someone in crisis is very real. You've done the right thing by pointing her toward professional help. How can we make sure you're also getting support?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I just feel helpless. But I have no desire to intervene myself. I'm not going to confront the guy or anything. I just wish there was more I could do for her.
